newsitem.title: USA: Motorola's Tooker to become chairman.
newsitem.headline: Motorola's Tooker to become chairman.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Thursday that William Weisz will retire as chairman of the board as of January 1 and Gary Tooker, currently vice chairman and chief executive, will replace him.

Weisz is retiring in accordance with the governance rules of the company's board of directors, which ask that no director stand for reelection following his or her 70th birthday, Motorola said. Weisz will be 70 in January.
Christopher Galvin will succeed Tooker as chief executive officer. He currently serves as president and chief operating officer.

The board elected Robert Growney to replace Galvin as president and chief operating officer. Growney has been executive vice president of Motorola and president and general manager of what is now the Messaging, Information and Media Sector since 1991.
To assist with the transition after January 1, Weisz will serve as vice chairman of the board, a position he held from 1980 to 1993, until he retires in May 1997, Motorola said.
As chairman, Tooker will remain an officer of Motorola. Weisz had retired from his active officership in 1989 and has served as chairman of the board since 1993, Motorola said.
Tooker, 57, said he had previously indicated to the board that he did not wish to serve as chief executive officer past the age of 60.
"I suggested that changes in both 1997, upon Bill's retirement, and again in 1999 were not in the best interests of the company nor its shareholders," Tooker said.

"Rather, I suggested that we look at Bill's retirement from the board as an opportunity to put a leadership team in place that would provide continuity into the 21st century," Tooker said. "I am very confident that we have just such a team."
Motorola said Tooker will focus on board governance issues and serve as an advisor to senior management. He also expects to represent Motorola outside the company.
Motorola said the board conducted a six-month chairman's succession study. That process concluded in a special meeting held Thursday morning, the company said.

"While it is true that Motorola has short-term problems that will, as we have noted previously, take a few quarters to resolve, I have every confidence that our efforts to implement sound cost controls and improve financial performance will be successful," Galvin said.
